title: Control Plane Version Governance and Staged Canary Upgrades for Private VPCs
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Goal: Implement a control plane version manager and a safe, automated staged-canary upgrade flow for Private (VPC) deployments. This ticket covers Terraform/IaC changes, the upgrade orchestration controller, health gating rules, automated rollback, and observability hooks required for production rollouts to customer VPCs. The feature must work with Dedicated/Private control plane variants and integrate with existing routing/fallback policies.

Background: Private customers run a customer-specific control plane inside their VPC or in an air-gapped on-prem setup. Upgrades today are manual and error-prone: operators sync versions, run scripted deploys, and follow runbooks. We need a repeatable, auditable, and safe automation path to: (1) pin/control control-plane component versions, (2) perform staged rollouts (canaries -> partial -> full), (3) gate by health and business metrics, and (4) provide automatic rollback and audit trail.

Scope: Terraform module changes to expose version variables and staged group resources, a lightweight upgrade-orchestrator service (k8s operator or controller) that performs staged upgrades via node-group/instance-set level updates, health gating ruleset and synthetic canary probes, integration with Console/observability for metrics/traces and rollout UI, and PRDs/documentation for SRE/SE-runbook handoffs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include deep DB schema migrations across customer clusters (that will be separate), nor does it cover multi-region cross-customer blue/green traffic split routing (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules expose control_plane_version and component_version variables with clear defaults and validation
A new orchestrator can apply staged upgrades: 1% canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with configurable pauses
Health gates defined (probe success rate >= 99%, p95 latency increase < 20%, error rate delta < 0.5%) and enforced at each stage
Automated rollback triggered when a gate fails; rollback documented and produces audit logs
Canary traffic uses synthetic requests and customer-like probe sets; results surfaced in Console rollout page
Upgrade run produces a machine-readable artifact (upgrade-report) with diffs, timings, checksums, and links to PRs/logs
E2E test deck that runs the upgrade flow against a staging VPC and includes failure injection scenarios
tasks: Design: finalize component versioning schema and compatibility matrix (api-server, reconciler, agent, control-plane-operator)
Terraform: add variables, validation, and staged_instance_group resources + examples in private-deployments modules
Orchestrator: implement staged-canary controller with pluggable gate evaluators (metrics, synthetic probes, custom webhooks)
Health checks: add synthetic probe suite and implement p95/p50 trackers and error slope detectors
Observability: wire rollout events to Console (rollout start/stop/stage/rollback), surface metrics and traces
CI: add smoke and canary-failure integration tests; add a dry-run mode to the orchestrator
Docs & Runbooks: update Private upgrade runbook, add Terraform examples and troubleshooting checklist
Security: run security review for the orchestrator's IAM/KMS access and document KMS patterns
notes: Meeting 2026-02-24: Agreed to implement the orchestrator as a small control-plane service (option 2) instead of a large operator to simplify upgrade window and cross-account permissions - notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Control+Plane+Upgrade+Options
SRE feedback (2026-02-28): require explicit pre-upgrade snapshot and post-upgrade reconciliation window (Marcus Liu)
PM note (Jonah Kim): customer-facing SLA wording and opt-out must be documented; some customers will require manual approval for stage transitions
Related infra tickets: ENG-9901 (private module refactor), ENG-10002 (canary metrics pipeline)
Initial gating thresholds proposed: success_rate >= 99%, error_rate_delta <= 0.5%, p95_latency_delta <= 20%

Playbook snippet: If canary fails stage-2, the orchestrator must: (1) stop rollout, (2) rollback canary nodes to previous version, (3) create incident and attach upgrade-report, (4) open follow-up PR to disable candidate version
